headline: First reading given to Merrimack Corridor TIF for 118 ACRE homes, with final vote set for December 8th
summary: Trinity Financial and the Lowell Housing Authority plan 90 units in a six-story building on Decatur Street and 28 units in a four-story building on Cabot Street. The developer's figures put net revenue to the city at about $6.9 million over the life of the tax deal. A second reading and final vote are planned for December 8th. Separately, cemetery fee changes were adopted and a traffic report on overnight parking was accepted.
decisions: Accepted the Merrimack Corridor Project motion response and placed it on file, 10-0.
Suspending the rules to give the Merrimack Corridor TIF a first reading failed, 7-3.
Appeal of the chair's ruling on the Merrimack Corridor TIF passed, 7-3.
First reading of the Merrimack Corridor TIF agreement passed, 7-3, with second reading at the December 8th meeting.
Adopted changes to the cemetery fee schedule ordinance, 10-0.
Referred Boston Gas's request to install approximately 1,515 ft of plastic gas main on Waugh, Bertha, and Wilder streets to the wire inspector, 10-0.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace about 100 ft of gas main between 304 and 330 West Sixth Street to the wire inspector, 10-0.
Referred National Grid's request for conduit to 681 Merrimack Street to the wire inspector, 10-0.
Referred the MassHire youth programming update to the Parks and Rec Subcommittee.
Approved a request for a report on using employees, trade students, and volunteers to upgrade the senior center, 10-0.
Approved a request to let NABET members give an update on LTC employment conditions.
Approved a report comparing city salaries with other gateway cities and nearby communities over five years.
Accepted the traffic ordinance amendments report, which covers overnight parking limits on University Ave and Riverside Street.
Accepted the Finance Subcommittee's November 17 report as a report of progress.
discussion: Merrimack Corridor TIF terms: Members questioned the 25 parking spaces, the $2,900 monthly rent for a three-bedroom unit, and the 2% yearly valuation increase used in the tax deal. The developer said the TIF is needed to pay a deferred developer fee within the 15-year tax compliance period.
Public comment on housing: Speakers mostly backed the 118 homes and the jobs they would bring. One speaker said the neighborhood was already crowded and asked about public safety and fire protection.

TIF vote timing: The developer said a vote was needed before the December 11th deadline, because HUD funding could be lost. Members argued whether a vote could be taken tonight, and the city solicitor said that depended on whether the deadline could be met at the next meeting.

LTC contract talks: Union members said the workers have gone more than three years without a raise and asked management to settle wages. A council member said both sides of the dispute should be heard.
Summer youth programs: Staff said 10 nonprofits could add 523 to 628 youth and 100 to 119 summer jobs, at an estimated median cost of $1,330.
